Call lambo_recall before acting on a task to load relevant prior memory, lambo_derive and lambo_record_action to write what you learned and did, lambo_reserve before editing a shared concept, and lambo_inspect / lambo_saints / lambo_stats to look around. A concept is one fact, stated atomically and short, such as a decision with its reason; it is not a log line or a paragraph, and activity goes to lambo_record_action. When a write rests on a ruling or decision recall showed you, cite it by its id (the 8 hex characters recall shows) in depends_on: lambo_record_action's, or the concept's on lambo_derive. When a write shows an existing concept to be wrong, name it the same way in against. Every tool takes your agent_id: use one stable id for as long as you run, never one per call, task or topic: your model or client id (<your-model-id>), with a stable instance suffix if several of you run at once. It is caller-asserted and unverified. Work is recorded under it, so a stable id keeps attribution whole. Soft locks are held under it: distinct ids contend for a node, and callers sharing an id share its locks and can release each other's, so concurrent agents that must keep out of each other's edits need distinct stable ids. created_at is server-stamped: do not send a client flush timestamp. lambo_derive and lambo_record_action may take optional RFC3339 event_time for historical about-time, such as a commit or document date; omit it for a live fact, which is about now. Ordering is yours to manage, and writes are applied in the BACKGROUND: lambo_derive and lambo_record_action return once your input is validated and ordered, and their ack carries a receipt id. Their outcome arrives on your next tool response. If you need a write visible to the very next read, call lambo_stats with that receipt and a wait_ms first; otherwise carry on — writes you send one after another are applied in that order (two you fire at once have no order to keep).
